seaweed-kelp-foods.name: Seaweed / kelp foods (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse — dried, as sold)

MeHg.control: Seaweed is a marine primary producer, not a predator; methylmercury does not biomagnify into algae, so MeHg is a negligible fraction of total mercury. Bounded by the tHg cell (Israel dried-seaweed tHg 2500): if tHg passes, MeHg is inherently far below any fish MeHg action level.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen (EPA 7473 / ICP-MS); reflex MeHg speciation (GC-ICP-MS, e.g. EPA 3200 / DIN EN 16801) only on a tHg exceedance.

Sn.control: Tin is a can-migration analyte, not a matrix-accumulation analyte. Dried seaweed foods (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse) are sold in non-metal packaging; with no tinplate contact there is no tin source. Every government tin ML in the register is either canned-product-only or an 'any food' catch-all set for can migration.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification on finished product.

shellfish.name: Shellfish (crustaceans and bivalve molluscs, not canned)

Sn.control: Tin is a can-migration analyte; not material for fresh/frozen shellfish placed on market without a tinplate container. Every government Sn ML for fishery products is a canned-only limit (MX/CR/IN 100-200 mg/kg). Reflex to the canned-seafood subcategory standard if the product is canned.

MeHg.label: No government sets a cephalopod-specific methylmercury ML. Read across from the non-predatory / general fishery MeHg value (Mexico NOM-242, other fishery products, 500 ug/kg): cephalopods are not high-trophic mercury accumulators, so the non-predatory fish MeHg tier is the nearest defensible value. Comparator vs any direct cephalopod MeHg limit.

Sn.control: Tin is a can-migration analyte; not material for fresh/frozen cephalopods placed on market without a tinplate container. Every government Sn ML for fishery products is a canned-only limit. Reflex to the canned-seafood subcategory standard if the product is canned.
Sn.reference_method: ICP-MS per EN 15763 / AOAC 2015.01; applies only if canned.

fish-freshwater.name: Freshwater fish (finfish) — tilapia, catfish, trout, carp

Sn.control: Fresh/frozen/refrigerated freshwater fish has no tinplate contact; inorganic tin is a canned-product migration pathway. Government Sn MLs for seafood (50-250 mg/kg) apply to canned product only. If the product is canned, it is certified under the canned-seafood subcategory Sn limit instead.
Sn.reference_method: ICP-MS per-lot screen; escalate to canned-seafood Sn limit if packaged in tinplate.

iAs.label: EU 2025/1891 inorganic arsenic 100 ug/kg for muscle meat of fish (species other than the listed higher-iAs group). No government sets an iAs ML specific to canned tuna; tuna is not in the EU listed-500 group, so it takes the general fish-muscle iAs floor.

fish-marine-non-predatory.name: Marine non-predatory fish (sardine, anchovy, salmon, cod, herring, mackerel; fillet/muscle meat, fresh or frozen)

Sn.control: canned-format gate: tin is regulated for seafood only as can/tinplate migration (MX 100000, CR/IN 200000 ug/kg, canned only); fresh/frozen fin-fish has no tin exposure pathway and no government sets a non-canned fish tin ML
Sn.reference_method: ICP-MS total tin on the edible portion; applies only if the product is canned (routed to the canned-seafood subcategory)

fish-marine-predatory.name: Marine predatory fish (tuna, swordfish, shark, king mackerel, marlin, billfish)

Sn.control: Tin is a can-migration analyte only: it enters food by dissolution from tinplate can walls, and fresh, frozen, or otherwise non-canned predatory fish (whole, fillet, loin, or portion) has no tin source. No government sets a tin ML for non-canned fish anywhere in the register; every seafood tin limit is scoped to canned/tinplate product and is excluded by the compiler's canned-gate for this non-canned subcategory. Canned predatory-fish products are certified under the canned-seafood subcategory, where the governing tin ceiling is the canned-food ML (Codex CXS 193 / GSO / India canned foods 250000 ug/kg; Chile canned fish and shellfish 250000 ug/kg). For non-canned product, tin is controlled by screen, not limited: any result above the reporting limit is investigated as evidence of unintended metal contact rather than an inherent property of the fish.
Sn.reference_method: Total Sn by ICP-MS or ICP-OES (e.g. AOAC 985.16 / EN 15764); screen threshold for non-canned product set at the method LOQ, with any quantifiable tin triggering a packaging/contact-material investigation.
